Docs/Reproducibility & submission

Reproducibility & submission

Prepare a reviewable experiment package while public leaderboard intake remains unavailable.

Current submission status

Preparation guide

The leaderboard shows the six manuscript baselines. Public community intake, hosted policy execution and independent submission verification are not available yet. This page documents the evidence needed to make a local comparison reproducible; it is not an upload portal.

First define which tracks you evaluated, freeze the policy and environment, and preserve the exact per-episode records from which your report is calculated.

Build the reproduction package

ArtifactInclude
Source and runtimeRepository/source revision, local changes, task fingerprint, adapter entry point, dependency versions and asset versions.
PolicyMethod name, checkpoint identity/hash, compatible model configuration, training budget and preprocessing.
DataDataset identity/revision, episode split, filtering, camera/state selection and training-data scope.
EnvironmentTask IDs, robot UIDs, action order, controller, backend, horizon, camera profile and instruction rule.
Episode manifestEvery planned task/background/seed tuple, stage-transition rule and worker assignment where applicable.
OutcomesPer-episode success, steps, stage trace, errors, logs, representative videos and the aggregation script.

Use stable local filenames and include a short explanation of how the files relate. If you distribute your own model or data, include its access instructions and actual license; the code repository's license does not automatically determine the terms of every asset.

Apply the declared evaluation units

Stage execution uses 50 episodes for each of 30 stages in the training scene. Cross-scene evaluation uses 50 episodes per stage in each of the three native kitchens with a frozen policy. Long-horizon evaluation uses 50 episodes per sequence, with one reset at the beginning and no resets between stages.

Weight stage tasks and complete sequences equally within their respective tracks. For cross-scene results, compute the stage average within each scene, then report the mean and standard deviation across the three scene averages. Scene standard deviation describes variation across scenes, not a confidence interval over training seeds.

Use matched episode seeds for a new method comparison and record the actual list. The paper's historical ACT/DP and GR00T runs use different recorded seed ranges; do not imply every manuscript method used identical seeds.

Check a result before sharing it

  1. Verify that every planned episode appears once and that partial runs are labeled.
  2. Recalculate the summary from raw episode records and check task weighting.
  3. Inspect representative successes and failures, including a complete-sequence rollout.
  4. Confirm that the report identifies the canonical embodiment and any deviations from the protocol.
  5. Provide the DexArena citation and original method references.

Use the score protocol for the reporting contract and Resources & release status for available public artifacts.
